prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1185; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a sideswipe during a lane change on a multi-lane road. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report and statements from two witnesses, both of whom describe the other vehicle drifting into the claimant's lane. Photographs taken at the scene show contact along the passenger-side panels, and the other driver's account matches the witnesses.

Entry 3: Inspected the claimed vehicle. The damage pattern is consistent with the described impact, and no earlier damage has come to light in the repair history or prior claims. Confirmed the driver listed on the declarations page is the person who was operating the vehicle at the time of loss.

Entry 4: Coverage was in force on the loss date, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date. Claimant reports neck and back strain and has provided medical records; no prior treatment to those body areas is documented.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has stayed the same across each recorded conversation, though it is still unclear from the statements exactly where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact. Treatment has followed a typical course and has been tapering as symptoms improve. Whether the injuries were caused by this collision has not yet been determined.

Entry 6: Reviewed the file with counsel's office and requested updated treatment notes to confirm the current status of the claimed injuries. Liability for the property damage appears clear, while the bodily injury component remains open pending medical causation review.
